diff --git a/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh b/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
index f9aa8c41..28684653 100755
--- a/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
+++ b/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
@@ -120,6 +120,649 @@
 # is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
 # =============================================================================
 
+# =============================================================================
+# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
+# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
+# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
+# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
+# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
+#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
+# under a caller's `set -u`.
+#
+# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
+# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
+# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
+# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
+# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
+# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
+# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
+# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
+# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
+#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
+#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
+#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
+#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
+#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
+#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
+#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
+#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
+#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
+#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
+#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
+#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
+#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
+#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
+#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
+#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
+#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
+#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
+#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
+#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
+#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
+#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
+#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
+#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
+#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
+#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
+#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
+#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
+#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
+#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
+#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
+#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
+# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
+# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
+# =============================================================================
+_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
+_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
+_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
+_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'
+_bdb_hd_re_rc='(^|/)\.(bashrc|bash_profile|bash_login|bash_logout|profile|zshrc|zshenv|zprofile|zlogin|zlogout|kshrc|mkshrc|cshrc|tcshrc|login|logout|envrc)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sedp='^(([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/)(,([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/))?)?p$'
+_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
+_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'
+_bdb_hd_re_knob='^[[:space:]]+heredoc_classifier:[[:space:]]*["'"'"']?([A-Za-z]+)["'"'"']?[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$'
+
+# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
+_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
+  case "$1" in
+    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
+    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;
+    sudo|doas|su|runuser|env|xargs|parallel|timeout|nohup|nice|ionice|setsid|stdbuf|chroot|unshare|nsenter|ssh|docker|podman|kubectl|find|watch|script) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
+_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
+  case "$1" in
+    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# Command words the fence's own rules match.
+_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
+  case "$1" in
+    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;
+    [Dd][Rr][Oo][Pp]|[Dd][Ee][Ll][Ee][Tt][Ee]|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Nn][Cc][Aa][Tt][Ee]) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
+_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
+  case "$1" in
+    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
+# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
+# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
+_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
+  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
+  n=${#s}
+  _bdb_hd_tok=()
+  while (( i < n )); do
+    ch="${s:i:1}"
+    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
+      tok="$tok$ch"
+      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
+        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
+        q=""
+      fi
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    case "$ch" in
+      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '\')
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
+      ' '|$'\t')
+        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
+        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '#')
+        (( have )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
+        op=""
+        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
+          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
+        done
+        i=$((i + ${#op}))
+        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
+          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        fi
+        if (( have )); then
+          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
+            op="$tok$op"
+          else
+            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+          fi
+          tok=""; have=0
+        fi
+        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
+      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
+  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
+# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
+_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
+  _hd_up=""
+  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
+    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
+    _hd_up="$1"
+  else
+    return 1
+  fi
+  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
+# content (or cannot be judged).
+_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
+  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
+  case "$p" in
+    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
+  b="${p##*/}"
+  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
+  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
+  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
+  else d="${PWD:-.}"
+  fi
+  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
+  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
+    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
+    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
+    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
+  done
+  IFS="$old_ifs"
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
+# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
+_bdb_hd_member() {
+  local -a toks argv
+  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
+  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()
+  _hd_mcls=none
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    t="${toks[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
+      case "$t" in
+        *'<<<') return ;;
+        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
+        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
+        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')
+          nxt="${toks[i+1]:-}"; i=$((i + 1))
+          if [[ -z "$nxt" || "$nxt" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+          case "$_hd_up" in /dev/null|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr) continue ;; esac
+          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
+          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
+          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))
+          continue ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+    fi
+    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
+  done
+  (( ${#argv[@]} > 0 )) || return
+  a0="${argv[0]}"
+  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"
+  if _bdb_hd_is_interp "$base" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$base"; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  [[ "$a0" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || return
+  (( stdout_files <= 1 )) || return
+  for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+    t="${argv[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  done
+  case "$a0" in
+    cat)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
+    tee)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -a|--append|-p) ;;
+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+             _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
+        esac
+      done ;;
+    echo|printf)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        case "${argv[i]}" in -n|-E) ;; -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    gh)
+      case "${argv[1]:-} ${argv[2]:-}" in
+        "pr comment"|"issue comment") want=" -F --body-file -R --repo |" ;;
+        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          --body-file=-) stdin=1 ;;
+          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+          -*)
+            if [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" $t "* ]]; then
+              i=$((i + 1))
+              [[ ( "$t" == "-F" || "$t" == "--body-file" ) && "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1
+            elif [[ "${want#*|}" != *" $t "* ]]; then
+              _hd_mcls=interpreter; return
+            fi ;;
+          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    git)
+      [[ "${argv[1]:-}" == commit ]] || return
+      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -F|--file) i=$((i + 1)); [[ "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; stdin=1 ;;
+          --file=-|-F-) stdin=1 ;;
+          -q|--quiet|-s|--signoff|-a|--all|--allow-empty|--allow-empty-message|-v|--verbose|--no-edit|--amend) ;;
+          *) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    br)
+      case "${argv[1]:-}" in create|update) ;; *) return ;; esac
+      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -d|--description|--body) [[ "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          --description=-|--body=-) stdin=1 ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    jq|yq)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        # In-place flags: --inplace/--in-place, -i, -i=…, and any short-flag cluster holding an i
+        # (corpus D114/D115: `-i` alone did not match `-[A-Za-z]*i*`, which needs a letter before the i).
+        case "${argv[i]}" in --inplace|--in-place|-i*|-[A-Za-z]*i*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    grep|egrep|fgrep) ;;
+    sed)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -n|--quiet|--silent) has_n=1 ;;
+          -E|-r|--regexp-extended|-s|--separate|-u|--unbuffered|-z|--null-data) ;;
+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) if [[ -z "$script" ]]; then
+               script="$t"; [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq || "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]] && script="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+               [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sedp ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+             fi ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( has_n )) && [[ -n "$script" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    sort)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -o) i=$((i + 1)); _bdb_hd_unq_path "${argv[i]:-}" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
+          -k|-t) i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+          -k*|-t*) ;;

+    if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]*'<<'-?$ ]]; then _hd_ops=$((_hd_ops + 1)); opi=$k; fi
+  done
+  (( _hd_ops == 1 )) || return
+  w="${_bdb_hd_tok[opi+1]:-}"
+  [[ "${_bdb_hd_tok[opi]}" == *'<<-' ]] && _hd_tabs=1
+  if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dsq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ddq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dbs ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _hd_quoted=1
+  elif [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dw ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="$w"
+  else
+    _hd_ops=-1; return        # variable-expanded, mixed or missing delimiter
+  fi
+  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"

+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
+  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
+  local cls=nonexec
+  k=0
+  while (( k < nt )); do
+    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi
+    mtoks=()
+    while (( k < nt )) && [[ "${tpipe[k]}" == "$_hd_pipe" ]]; do mtoks[${#mtoks[@]}]="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"; k=$((k + 1)); done
+    _bdb_hd_member "${mtoks[@]}"

+      interpreter) cls=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$cls" == interpreter ]] || cls=none ;;
+    esac
+    k=$((k + 1))
+  done
+  _hd_cls="$cls"

+
+# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
+# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
+_bdb_hd_segword() {
+  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
+  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""
+  while (( guard < 64 )); do
+    guard=$((guard + 1))
+    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+    [[ -n "$s" ]] || return
+    case "${s:0:1}" in
+      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"
+    s="${s:${#w}}"
+    if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_assign ]]; then continue; fi
+    case "$w" in
+      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)
+        while :; do
+          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+          case "$s" in
+            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
+            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)
+              s="${s:2}"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            -*) w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            *) break ;;
+          esac
+        done
+        continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${w%%[\"\']*}"
+    [[ "$w" == */* && "$w" != '$'* ]] && w="${w##*/}"
+    _hd_w="$w"; _hd_rest="$s"
+    return
+  done

+
+# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
+# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
+# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
+# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
+_bdb_hd_scan_body() {
+  local k l t seg
+  _hd_kept="" _hd_synth="" _hd_full=0
+  for ((k = $1; k <= $2; k++)); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[k]}"
+    [[ "$l" == *'<<'* ]] && _hd_full=1
+    if (( ! $3 )); then
+      case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) _hd_full=1 ;; esac
+    fi
+    t="${l//'&&'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'||'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'|'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//';'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'&'/$'\n'}"
+    while :; do
+      seg="${t%%$'\n'*}"
+      _bdb_hd_segword "$seg"
+      if [[ -n "$_hd_w" ]]; then
+        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
+          _hd_full=1
+          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_full=1
+        fi
+      fi
+      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
+      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
+    done
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
+# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
+# reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
+_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
+  local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
+  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
+    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue
+    [[ "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" == *"$b"* ]] || continue
+    _bdb_hd_tokenize "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" || return 0
+    nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
+    start=0 pipe=0
+    for ((j = 0; j <= nt; j++)); do
+      t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
+      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi
+      # segment [start, j)
+      own=0
+      (( k == hi && pipe == _hd_pipe_saved )) && own=1
+      if (( ! own )); then
+        seg_has=0 cw=""
+        for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
+          u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
+          [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
+        done
+        if (( seg_has )); then
+          _bdb_hd_segword "${_bdb_hd_tok[*]:start:j-start}"
+          cw="$_hd_w"
+          if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
+        fi
+      fi
+      case "$t" in '|'|'|&') ;; *) pipe=$((pipe + 1)) ;; esac
+      start=$((j + 1))
+    done
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc
+# bodies reduced to their fence-verb segments) and set _bdb_hd_class to the
+# most executing class seen (interpreter > none > nonexec; none if no heredoc).
+_bdb_heredoc_scrub() {
+  local text="${1:-}" out="" i j found l cls ctx=0 seen="" d first
+  _bdb_hd_class=none
+  text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"
+  if [[ "$text" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ctl ]]; then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+  text="${text%$'\n'}"
+  _bdb_hd_L=()
+  while IFS= read -r l; do _bdb_hd_L[${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}]="$l"; done <<< "$text"
+  _bdb_hd_n=${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}
+  i=0
+  while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"
+    if [[ "$l" != *'<<'* ]]; then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_header "$l"
+    if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    found=-1
+    for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
+      d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
+      if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
+      if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
+    done
+    if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    cls="$_hd_cls"
+    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
+    _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
+      (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
+      first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
+      [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
+    fi
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      local -a dests
+      dests=(${_hd_dests[@]+"${_hd_dests[@]}"})
+      for d in ${dests[@]+"${dests[@]}"}; do
+        if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then
+          cls=interpreter; break
+        fi
+      done
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_scan_body $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)) "$_hd_quoted"
+    out="$out$l"$'\n'
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && (( ! _hd_full )); then
+      # #1245 special case: a standalone quoted `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops it all.
+      if ! (( i == 0 && found == _bdb_hd_n - 1 && _hd_quoted )) || ! _bdb_hd_plain_cat "$l"; then
+        out="$out$_hd_kept"
+      fi
+    else
+      [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && cls=interpreter
+      for ((j = i + 1; j < found; j++)); do out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"$'\n'; done
+      out="$out$_hd_synth"
+    fi
+    out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[found]}"$'\n'
+    (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+    case "$cls" in
+      interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
+      nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
+    esac
+    i=$((found + 1))
+  done
+  _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
+  printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
+}
+
+# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
+_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
+  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
+  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
+  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
+  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"
+  [[ "$header" =~ $delimiter_re ]] || return 1
+  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
+  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
+  [[ "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]
+}
+
+# Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's
+# .loa.config.yaml (read once, no fork, only for commands holding `<<`).
+# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
+_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
+  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
+  [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0
+  IFS= read -r -d '' content < "$cfg" || true
+  [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r l; do
+    case "$l" in
+      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
+      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
+    esac
+    if (( in_blk )) && [[ "$l" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_knob ]]; then
+      case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
+    fi
+  done <<< "$content"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
+_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  local LC_ALL=C
+  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null
+  printf '%s\n' "$_bdb_hd_class"
+}
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}
+
+# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs
+# normally — an environment variable can never switch the fence off.
+if [[ "${BDB_LIB_ONLY:-}" == "1" && "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0:-}" ]]; then
+  return 0
+fi
+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Invariant 4b: optional constraint tables appear exactly when their class has
+# rows (cycle-129 D-4.5). generate-constraints.sh omits the "## Agent Teams"
+# table when constraints.json has no agent_teams_constraints rows; the kernel
+# must then carry neither the heading nor the marker, and must carry the
+# marker whenever the rows exist.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+check_optional_constraint_tables() {
+  local file=".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" registry=".claude/data/constraints.json"
+  [[ -f "$file" && -f "$registry" ]] || return 0
+  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  jq empty "$registry" 2>/dev/null || return 0   # invariant 3 reports invalid JSON
+
+  local entry section heading rows has_marker has_heading
+  for entry in "agent_teams_constraints|## Agent Teams"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r section heading <<< "$entry"
+    rows=$(jq --arg s "$section" '[.constraints[]? | select(any(.layers[]?; .section == $s))] | length' "$registry" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    has_marker=0; has_heading=0
+    grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section} " "$file" 2>/dev/null && has_marker=1
+    grep -qxF "$heading" "$file" 2>/dev/null && has_heading=1
+    if [[ "$rows" -eq 0 && ( "$has_marker" -eq 1 || "$has_heading" -eq 1 ) ]]; then
+      report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "${section}: constraints.json has no rows but CLAUDE.loa.md still carries the '${heading}' table — run generate-constraints.sh"
+    elif [[ "$rows" -gt 0 && "$has_marker" -eq 0 ]]; then
+      report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "${section}: constraints.json has ${rows} row(s) but CLAUDE.loa.md has no ${section} block — restore the '${heading}' heading block, then run generate-constraints.sh"
+    else
+      report "PASS" "constraint-blocks" "${section}: table presence matches constraints.json (${rows} row(s))"
+    fi
+  done
+}

+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. +- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
+# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
+# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
+# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
+# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
+#
+#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
+#                                           all have non-executing consumers
+#
+# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
+# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
+# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
+_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
+fi
+unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
+
+heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
+  else
+    printf 'none\n'
+  fi
+}
+
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}

+# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
+# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
+# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
+# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
+fb_parse() {
+  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
+  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
+  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
+  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
+  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
+  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
+  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
+  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
+  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
+    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
+  else
+    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
+  fi
+  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
+    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
+    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
+    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
+     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
+     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
+     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
+    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
+}

+# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
+# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
+impl_commit() {
+  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
+    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
+    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
+}

+# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
+# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
+rounds_of() {
+  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
+  for g in review audit; do
+    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
+    top=""; topn=-1
+    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
+      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
+      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
+      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
+      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
+      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
+    done
+    cur="$dir/$base.md"
+    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
+      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
+    fi
+  done
+}

+# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
+JQ_DEFS='
+def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
+def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
+def recompute($rounds; $reset):
+  ($rounds
+   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
+   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
+   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
+  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
+      .cycle += 1
+      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
+      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
+      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
+      | .lc = $c);
+def skeleton($th; $ts):
+  {state: "CLOSED",
+   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
+              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
+              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
+              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
+   history: []};
+def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
+  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
+  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
+  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
+     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
+  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
+     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
+          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
+  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
+      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
+      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
+      else null end ) as $trip
+  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
+    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
+def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
+def resolve($f; $now; $win):
+  . as $c
+  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
+  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
+  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
+  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
+      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
+      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
+  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
+  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
+    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
+    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
+    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
+    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
+    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
+'

+cmd_derive() {
+  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows

+    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4

+cmd_record_round() {
+  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
+  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
+  local p th ts now out trip
+  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
+  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
+    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
+  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
+      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
+      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
+    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
+  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
+  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
+  echo "$out"
+  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
+    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
+    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_mark() {
+  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
+  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
+  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
+    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
+  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+    local err drc=0
+    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
+    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
+  fi
+  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
+}
+

-  write) cmd_write ;;
-  read)  cmd_read ;;
+  write)  cmd_write ;;
+  read)   cmd_read ;;
+  derive) cmd_derive ;;
+  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
+  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
+  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
   *) usage ;;
 esac

+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Profile (cycle-129, DEC-0143)
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# One knob sets the defaults of the optional surfaces as a set:
+#   known_failures.surface_at_session_start, decisions.surface_at_session_start,
+#   karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning,
+#   karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria, guardrails.input.enabled,

+#   structured_handoff.enabled, soul_identity_doc.enabled
+# `lean` turns them all off, `full` all on, and `standard` (the default) is the
+# per-key default this file shows (soul_identity_doc.enabled, not shown here,
+# is false). A key you set explicitly anywhere in
+# this file wins over the profile. The values per profile live in
+# .claude/data/profiles.yaml; `/loa` prints the effective profile and your
+# explicit overrides. No floor key is reachable through a profile: review,
+# audit, verdict-derive, the dissent artefact gate, the deny list, the
+# destructive-command fence, the System-Zone rules and every other floor
+# config key read the same configuration under every profile
+# (.claude/data/floor.yaml lists them; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats pins it).
+# An unknown value warns and falls back to standard.
+loa:
+  profile: standard   # lean | standard | full
+

 # Ride Configuration (v1.31.0)
 # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
@@ -551,6 +574,16 @@ run_mode:
   defaults:

+  # .run/circuit-breaker.json from COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger

+  # the rollback key).
+  file_authoritative: true
+  # Hours after which a RUNNING run with no activity derives to INTERRUPTED, and after
+  # which a derived cache (derived_at) no longer counts as a known run position for the
+  # implement gate. Positive integer.
+  stale_hours: 12

     branch_prefix: "feature/"

+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Implement gate (cycle-129 FR-4(a); hook: .claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh)
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# PreToolUse check on Write/Edit/NotebookEdit into the App Zone (src/, lib/, app/)
+# outside an implementation run. A write is SANCTIONED (allowed, one audit row each) by:
+#   - a RUNNING run cache (.run/sprint-plan-state.json or .run/state.json, fresh
+#     last_activity, and derived_at within run_mode.stale_hours when present);
+#   - .run/implement-active.json {skill: implement|bug, sprint, started_at} younger than
+#     two hours (`run-checkpoint.sh mark` at the start of /implement and /bug, `unmark`
+#     at the end); a stale or malformed marker is logged and does not sanction;
+#   - LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the session environment (audited, one row per write).
+# An unsanctioned App-Zone write is then handled by `mode`:
+#   ask        (default) asks for confirmation, as before, and logs one row per ask
+#   telemetry  logs one row to .run/audit.jsonl and allows silently
+#   deny       refuses the write when the derived run position is known (the cache parses
+#              and its derived_at is within run_mode.stale_hours); an unknown position
+#              (missing, not derived, stale, unparseable) asks instead, never allows.
+#              The hook is a fence only in this mode.
+# Writes to the gate's own inputs (.run state files, .run/audit.jsonl, the marker,
+# .loa.config.yaml) ask in every mode and under every sanction.
+# `claims: authoritative` is a tighten-only modifier for any mode: a model-authored
+# tool_input.active_skill naming a non-implementation skill asks (or, under deny, is
+# denied), and never allows by itself. The legacy `mode: authoritative` means
+# mode: ask + claims: authoritative. /loa prints the effective mode on its Gate line.

# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — this hook must never fail closed.
# A grep or jq failure must result in exit 0 (allow), not an error.
#
# WHY fail-open (not fail-closed): A safety hook that crashes or encounters
# a parse error must NOT block the agent from operating. The alternative —
# fail-closed — would make jq/grep bugs into denial-of-service attacks
# against the agent. Fail-open with logging is the standard pattern for
# inline security hooks (cf. ModSecurity DetectionOnly mode).
# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix)
#
# WHY GNU/BSD ERE (NOT strict POSIX): grep -P (PCRE) is a GNU extension not
# available on macOS/BSD or minimal containers. grep -E (Extended Regex)
# with `\s`, `\S`, `\b` extensions works on both GNU grep (Linux) and BSD
# grep (macOS Sonoma+). Strict-POSIX ERE (busybox without -E extensions)
# is NOT in scope per cycle-111 SDD §5.0 honest-scope decision.
# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix; cycle-111 SDD §5.0)
#
# WHY single script for all patterns: NFR-5 single-file invariant. Multiple
# hooks would each read stdin, parse JSON, and run regex — multiplying
# latency per command. A single emit_block helper with sequential patterns
# is simpler and faster. (cycle-111 SDD §5/§6.)
#
# Defense-in-depth posture (cycle-111 SDD §11): this hook is a fence
# against routine destructive-command mistakes by autonomous agents, NOT
# a hardened security boundary against intentional bypass. Known accepted
# bypass classes: newline statement separators, subshell wrapping
# (`bash -c '...'`, `$(...)`), eval/base64 decode, SQL comments containing
# WHERE, jq absent from PATH. See SDD §11 for full table.
# Current executable limit examples and issue dispositions:
# docs/runbooks/hook-safety.md (#1047, #1245, #1088, #1031).
#
# cycle-125 FR-1 (2026-09-23) — precision pass against the fleet corpus
# (tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/, replayed by tests/unit/block-destructive-
# bash.bats). Relaxations, each on a positively established predicate:
# FR-2 cache/build vocabulary by last segment, bare names after a
# statement-initial `cd <temp>`, paths strictly below /tmp|/var/tmp|
# /private/tmp, `$TMPDIR/<name>` only with a real temp TMPDIR, a variable
# bound exactly once to `$(mktemp -d)`; FR-1.1 branches that are ancestors
# of main/master (offline `git merge-base`); FR-1.3 generated paths;
# FR-1.4/5/6 only when a SQL runner (psql, mysql, sqlite3, prisma, …) or an
# inline interpreter program (`python -c`, `node -e`) is in the command.
# ACCEPTED RESIDUALS (deliberately not relaxed):
#   * Remote payloads: `ssh host 'rm -rf /'`, `docker exec c rm -rf /data`,
#     `kubectl exec p -- rm -rf /` keep blocking. A scrub of quoted remote

+# mode {unset, ask, telemetry, deny} × claims {plain, authoritative} × write {app, trust}
+# × sanction {none, run_fresh, run_stale, marker_fresh, marker_stale, override}
+# × cache {fresh, stale, missing, unparseable} (run_* sanctions define the cache themselves)
+# =============================================================================
+
+# $1 mode (unset = no key) $2 claims (plain | authoritative)
+cfg_gate() {
+    : > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    if [[ "$1" != unset || "$2" == authoritative ]]; then
+        printf 'implement_gate:\n' >> "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+        [[ "$1" != unset ]] && printf '  mode: %s\n' "$1" >> "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+        [[ "$2" == authoritative ]] && printf '  claims: authoritative\n' >> "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    fi
+    return 0
+}
+
+# $1 cache: fresh | stale | missing | unparseable | run_fresh | run_stale (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
+cache_state() {
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    case "$1" in
+        missing) ;;
+        unparseable) printf '{"state": "RUNNING", \n' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        fresh)     jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", status: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        stale)     jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", status: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now - 13 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        run_fresh) jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "RUNNING", status: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        run_stale) jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "RUNNING", status: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now - 13 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# $1 sanction: none | marker_fresh | marker_stale | override (run_* handled by cache_state); echoes the override value
+marker_state() {
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json"
+    case "$1" in
+        marker_fresh) jq -nc '{skill: "implement", sprint: "sprint-256", started_at: (now | floor | todate)}' > "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json" ;;
+        marker_stale) jq -nc '{skill: "bug", sprint: "sprint-bug-9", started_at: (now - 3 * 3600 | floor | todate)}' > "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json" ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# $1 path $2 claims $3 override (1 or empty) — stdout/stderr split, LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
+gate_cell() {
+    if [[ "$2" == authoritative ]]; then
+        jq -nc --arg p "$1" '{tool_name: "Write", tool_input: {file_path: $p, content: "x", active_skill: "review-sprint"}}' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    else
+        jq -nc --arg p "$1" '{tool_name: "Write", tool_input: {file_path: $p, content: "x"}}' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    fi
+    run --separate-stderr env -u LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE ${3:+LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=$3} LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 \
+        bash -c 'cd "$1" && PROJECT_ROOT="$1" RUN_DIR="$1/.run" bash "$2" < "$3"' _ "$ROOT" "$GATE" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+}
+
+# allow | ask | deny | invalid:<stdout>
+decision3() {
+    if [[ -z "$output" ]]; then echo allow; return; fi
+    local d
+    d=$(jq -r 'if (has("decision") | not) and .hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName == "PreToolUse"
+                  and (.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason | type == "string" and length > 0)
+               then .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision else "invalid" end' <<<"$output" 2>/dev/null) || d=invalid
+    case "$d" in ask|deny) echo "$d" ;; *) echo "invalid:$output" ;; esac
+}
+
+# The expected "<decision> <row>" for one cell; row = action/decision of the write's decision row
+expect_cell() {
+    local mode="$1" claims="$2" wclass="$3" sanction="$4" cache="$5" sanctioned=0 known=0
+    [[ "$mode" == unset ]] && mode=ask
+    if [[ "$wclass" == trust ]]; then echo "ask ask/trust_input"; return; fi
+    case "$sanction" in run_fresh|marker_fresh|override) sanctioned=1 ;; esac
+    case "$cache" in fresh|run_fresh) known=1 ;; esac
+    if [[ "$claims" == authoritative ]]; then
+        if [[ "$mode" == deny ]] && (( ! sanctioned && known )); then echo "deny deny/deny"; else echo "ask ask/ask"; fi
+        return
+    fi
+    if (( sanctioned )); then
+        case "$sanction" in run_fresh) echo "allow allow/sanctioned_run" ;; marker_fresh) echo "allow allow/sanctioned_marker" ;; *) echo "allow allow/override" ;; esac
+        return
+    fi
+    case "$mode" in
+        ask) echo "ask ask/ask" ;;
+        telemetry) echo "allow telemetry/outside_run" ;;
+        deny) if (( known )); then echo "deny deny/deny"; else echo "ask ask/unknown_position"; fi ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# Runs every claims × write × sanction × cache cell for one mode and checks decision, row, row count, replay flag
+run_mode_matrix() {
+    local mode="$1" claims wclass sanction cache path got want row rows n_note n
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"
+    for claims in plain authoritative; do
+        cfg_gate "$mode" "$claims"
+        for wclass in app trust; do
+            if [[ "$wclass" == app ]]; then path="$ROOT/src/x.ts"; else path="$ROOT/.run/state.json"; fi
+            for sanction in none run_fresh run_stale marker_fresh marker_stale override; do
+                for cache in fresh stale missing unparseable; do
+                    case "$sanction" in run_*) [[ "$cache" == fresh ]] || continue; cache="$sanction" ;; esac
+                    cache_state "$cache"; marker_state "$sanction"
+                    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+                    gate_cell "$path" "$claims" "$([[ "$sanction" == override ]] && echo 1)"
+                    local cell="mode=$mode claims=$claims write=$wclass sanction=$sanction cache=$cache"
+                    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$cell: exit $status" >&2; return 1; }
+                    want=$(expect_cell "$mode" "$claims" "$wclass" "$sanction" "$cache")
+                    got="$(decision3)"
+                    [ "$got" = "${want%% *}" ] || { echo "$cell: expected ${want%% *}, got $got" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # the write's decision row: the claim row (model_signal), the trust row (state_write) or the gate row
+                    row=$(jq -sr 'map(select(.action != "note" and (.hook == "implement-gate"))) | if length == 1 then "\(.[0].action)/\(.[0].decision)" else "count:\(length)" end' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null) || row="no-rows"
+                    [ "$row" = "${want#* }" ] || { echo "$cell: expected row ${want#* }, got $row" >&2; cat "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # a stale marker logs stale_marker (and never sanctions) whenever the run path did not sanction first
+                    n_note=$(jq -s 'map(select(.decision == "stale_marker")) | length' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl")
+                    if [[ "$wclass" == app && "$sanction" == marker_stale ]]; then
+                        [ "$n_note" = 1 ] || { echo "$cell: expected one stale_marker row, got $n_note" >&2; return 1; }
+                    else
+                        [ "$n_note" = 0 ] || { echo "$cell: unexpected stale_marker row" >&2; return 1; }
+                    fi
+                    # every row this gate wrote carries replay: true under LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 (DEC-0167)
+                    n=$(jq -s 'map(select(.replay != true)) | length' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl")
+                    [ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "$cell: $n rows without replay: true" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # telemetry prints nothing at all
+                    if [[ "${want#* }" == telemetry/outside_run ]]; then
+                        [[ -z "$output" && -z "$stderr" ]] || { echo "$cell: telemetry printed something" >&2; return 1; }
+                    fi
+                done
+            done
+        done
+    done
+}
+
+@test "IG-24 matrix, implement_gate unset: behaves exactly as ask in every cell" {
+    run_mode_matrix unset
+}
+
+@test "IG-25 matrix, mode ask: unsanctioned App-Zone writes ask with one ask row; sanctions allow with their own row; trust inputs ask" {
+    run_mode_matrix ask
+}
+
+@test "IG-26 matrix, mode telemetry: an unsanctioned App-Zone write logs one outside_run row and prints nothing; a non-implementation claim still asks" {
+    run_mode_matrix telemetry
+}
+
+@test "IG-27 matrix, mode deny: deny only for an unsanctioned App-Zone write with a fresh derived cache; an unknown position asks; trust inputs ask" {
+    run_mode_matrix deny
+}
+
+@test "IG-28 the telemetry row has exactly the documented keys and a control-stripped path of at most 256 bytes; without LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY no replay key" {
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"

+    jq -nc --arg p "$ROOT/src/a"$'\x1b'"[31mb.ts" '{tool_name: "Write", tool_input: {file_path: $p, content: "x"}}' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    run --separate-stderr env -u LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY -u LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE bash -c 'cd "$1" && PROJECT_ROOT="$1" RUN_DIR="$1/.run" bash "$2" < "$3"' _ "$ROOT" "$GATE" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ -z "$output" ]
+    [ -z "$stderr" ]
+    run jq -c 'keys' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    [ "$output" = '["action","decision","hook","mode","path","ts"]' ]
+    run jq -r '[.hook, .action, .decision, .mode, .path] | join(" ")' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    [ "$output" = "implement-gate telemetry outside_run telemetry $ROOT/src/a[31mb.ts" ]
+    run -1 env LC_ALL=C grep -q $'[\x01-\x09\x0b-\x1f\x7f]' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    local long
+    long=$(printf 'k%.0s' {1..400})
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    jq -nc --arg p "$ROOT/src/$long.ts" '{tool_name: "Write", tool_input: {file_path: $p, content: "x"}}' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    run --separate-stderr env -u LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY bash -c 'cd "$1" && PROJECT_ROOT="$1" RUN_DIR="$1/.run" bash "$2" < "$3"' _ "$ROOT" "$GATE" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    run jq -j '.path' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    [ "$(printf '%s' "$output" | LC_ALL=C wc -c)" -le 256 ]

+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
+# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
+#
+# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
+# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
+# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
+# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
+# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
+# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
+# =============================================================================
+
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
+    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
+    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
+    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
+    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
+    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
+    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
+    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
+    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
+    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
+    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
+    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
+    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
+    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
+    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
+}
+
+# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
+checkpoint() {
+    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
+        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
+          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
+        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+}
+
+# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
+write_lines() {
+    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
+    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
+    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
+        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
+        | bash "$HOOK"
+}
+
+@test "KS-1 the counter resets when the checkpoint task changes" {
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-aaa
+    write_lines 3
+    write_lines 2
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-aaa" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "5" ]
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-bbb
+    write_lines 2
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-bbb" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.over' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl")" -eq 2 ]
+    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-bbb.jsonl")" -eq 1 ]
+    [ "$(tail -1 "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl" | jq -r '.running_total')" = "5" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-2 with no run in progress the key is the payload's session id, then LOA_SESSION_ID" {
+    write_lines 1 "abc-123"
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/abc-123.jsonl" ]

+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-open.jsonl" ]
+    # A sprint-granularity checkpoint (no task) keys on the sprint too.
+    checkpoint sprint-257
+    write_lines 1
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "sprint-257" ]

diff --git a/tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats b/tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..475bc1ab
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats — cycle-129 D-4.5 (AC-2.5)
+#
+# The five C-TEAM rows left constraints.json; generate-constraints.sh omits the
+# "## Agent Teams" table when the class is empty and renders it when rows
+# exist; lint-invariants.sh fails when the kernel and the registry disagree.
+# The generator runs against a fixture tree (it resolves its inputs relative
+# to the working directory), never against the live kernel.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    GEN="$R/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh"
+    LINT="$R/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh"
+    F="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/tree"
+    mkdir -p "$F/.claude/loa" "$F/.claude/data" "$F/.claude/templates"
+    cp -R "$R/.claude/templates/constraints" "$F/.claude/templates/constraints"
+    cp "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+    cp "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+# A kernel that still carries the pre-cycle-129 Agent Teams block, placed
+# between the merge constraints and the Agent-Network section as it was.
+add_team_block() {
+    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
+import sys
+p = sys.argv[1]
+s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
+anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"
+block = ("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n"
+         "<!-- @constraint-generated: start agent_teams_constraints | hash:0000000000000000 -->\n"
+         "<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->\n"
+         "| MUST stale row | stale |\n"
+         "<!-- @constraint-generated: end agent_teams_constraints -->\n\n")
+assert s.count(anchor) == 1
+open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(anchor, block + anchor))
+PY
+}
+
+add_team_row() {
+    jq '.constraints += [{"id":"C-TEAM-901","name":"fixture_row","category":"agent_teams","rule_type":"MUST",
+        "text":"fixture rule","text_variants":{"claude-loa-md":"MUST fixture rule"},"why":"fixture why","order":0,
+        "layers":[{"target":"claude-loa-md","section":"agent_teams_constraints","render_as":"table_row"}],
+        "severity":"low","source_incident":"#0"}]' "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json" > "$F/c.json"
+    mv "$F/c.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+}
+
+gen() { (cd "$F" && bash "$GEN" --section "${1:-agent_teams_constraints}"); }
+
+@test "LI-1 constraints.json carries no C-TEAM rows and no agent_teams_constraints layer" {
+    run jq '[.constraints[] | select((.id | startswith("C-TEAM")) or any(.layers[]?; .section == "agent_teams_constraints"))] | length' \
+        "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$output" = "0" ]
+}
+
+@test "LI-2 the live kernel carries neither the Agent Teams heading nor its marker" {
+    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-3 the generator removes a leftover Agent Teams block when the class is empty" {
+    add_team_block
+    grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    # The neighbouring sections survive with one blank line between them.
+    grep -qF '<!-- @constraint-generated: end merge_constraints -->' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    run grep -c '^## Agent-Network Primitives$' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    [ "$output" = "1" ]
+    run diff <(sed -n '/end merge_constraints/,/^## Agent-Network/p' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md") \
+             <(printf '%s\n' '<!-- @constraint-generated: end merge_constraints -->' '' '## Agent-Network Primitives')
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "LI-4 pruning is idempotent: a second run leaves the kernel byte-identical" {
+    add_team_block
+    gen
+    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/first.md"
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    cmp "$F/first.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-5 the generator renders the table when the class has rows" {
+    add_team_block
+    add_team_row
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    grep -qxF '| MUST fixture rule | fixture why |' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    ! grep -qF 'MUST stale row' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-6 rows without the heading block fail loudly and leave the kernel untouched" {
+    add_team_row
+    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Missing markers"*"agent_teams_constraints"* ]]
+    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-7 a marker block with foreign text above it is an error, not a silent deletion" {
+    add_team_block
+    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
+import sys
+p = sys.argv[1]
+s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
+s = s.replace("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |", "## Agent Teams\n\nOperator prose that is not a table.\n\n| Rule | Why |")
+open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
+PY
+    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"
+    run gen
+    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"no '## Agent Teams' heading directly above its table"* ]]
+    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+@test "LI-8 lint-invariants passes the optional-table invariant on the live tree" {
+    run bash -c "cd '$R' && bash '$LINT' --json"
+    echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.message | test("agent_teams_constraints: table presence matches"))' >/dev/null
+    ! echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.level == "ERROR" and (.message | test("agent_teams")))' >/dev/null
+    # The field name is load-bearing: the negative check above is vacuous if
+    # the report shape ever renames `level`.
+    echo "$output" | jq -e '[.results[] | has("level")] | all' >/dev/null
+}
+
+@test "LI-9 the lint self-test (test-lint-invariants.sh) is green" {
+    run bash -c "cd '$R' && bash .claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh"
+    echo "$output" | tail -3
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}

+++ b/tests/unit/profile-floor.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,200 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/profile-floor.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
+# AC-9.2; SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166)
+#
+# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
+# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
+# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot
+# disagree. Under `lean` every floor surface reads byte-identically to
+# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
+# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
+# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's
+# decision and environment, the deny-list file, the fence on the corpus and
+# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.
+# =============================================================================
+
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
+    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+    FLOOR="$R/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    # Two configs that differ ONLY in loa.profile: this repository's own config
+    # (which carries the floor keys it really uses) with the profile set.
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        cp "$R/.loa.config.yaml" "$T/$p.yaml"
+        yq -i ".loa.profile = \"$p\"" "$T/$p.yaml"
+    done
+    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE LOA_PROFILES_FILE
+}
+
+# The floor key patterns, as the lib and the guard register read them.
+floor_keys() { yq -r '.floor_keys[]' "$FLOOR"; }
+
+@test "PF-1 floor.yaml matches the sha256 pin guard-origins.bats carries (one constant, two suites)" {
+    local pin actual
+    pin=$(sed -n 's/^FLOOR_SHA256="\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)"$/\1/p' "$R/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats")
+    [ -n "$pin" ] || { echo "no FLOOR_SHA256 in guard-origins.bats"; return 1; }
+    actual=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$2"' _ "$R" "$FLOOR" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+    [ "$actual" = "$pin" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $pin"; return 1; }
+}
+
+@test "PF-2 no profiles.yaml key matches a floor key or is an ancestor of one" {
+    run python3 -I - "$PROFILES" "$FLOOR" <<'PY'
+import re, subprocess, sys, json
+def load(p):
+    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["yq", "-o=json", ".", p]))
+prof, floor = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
+keys = sorted({k for v in prof["profiles"].values() for k in v})
+assert len(keys) == 9, keys
+bad = []
+for k in keys:
+    for f in floor["floor_keys"]:
+        rx = "^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in f.split("*")) + "$"
+        if re.match(rx, k) or f.split("*")[0].startswith(k + "."):
+            bad.append((k, f))
+print("violations:", bad)
+sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
+PY
+    echo "$output"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    # floor_keys_forbidden is not duplicated into profiles.yaml.
+    [ "$(yq -r 'has("floor_keys_forbidden")' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
+}
+
+@test "PF-3 under lean the resolved document names no floor key and every floor key reads as under standard" {
+    local p k
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$LIB" json > "$T/$p.json"
+        [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/$p.json")" = "$p" ]
+    done
+    # Concrete floor keys: every leaf path of this config and the example that a

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"
